MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "The USB extension cable offers a practical way to make peripherals easier to reach, which fits my history of buying connection accessories, though USB 2.0 limits its usefulness with my USB 3.0 equipment.",
    "The Edimax adapter fits my interest in USB networking and resembles my Panda adapter, so it feels relevant even though I would skip it because it duplicates something I already have."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "The memory cards and hard drives address storage needs I have not expressed; sharing a USB connection with my accessories does not give me a reason to buy storage now.",
    "My Ethernet adapter purchase does not establish a need to replace my modem or extend Wi-Fi coverage, and either purchase would require a specific problem to solve.",
    "My tablet mount and headset do not give me a current reason to buy an action camera or share audio through a splitter."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "The recommendations seem to treat a shared connection type as evidence of a shared purpose, even when the products solve very different problems.",
    "They seem to turn ownership of an accessory into an assumed need for related equipment, without a clear reason for me to buy it."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "My purchases are infrequent and concern specific practical needs, so a loosely related device is unlikely to prompt me to interact.",
    "An item can match my interests yet duplicate equipment I already own, as the Edimax adapter does.",
    "My most recent purchase supports interest in connecting a computer through Ethernet, while my USB 3.0 equipment makes connection speed relevant when choosing cables."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The recommendations partly recognize my interest in connectivity accessories but infer too many new equipment needs from that interest."
}
